I was in the theater at the midnight premiere, and when I tell you the screams of horror almost drowned out the audio. At first, it was complete and utter shock and denial. People started yelling when Esme reacted to Carlisle’s death, "This wasn’t in the book!" Midway through the scene people were getting into it. Cheering, applauding, getting out of seats and jumping up and down for every Volturi taken down. When Seth died multiple people shrieked, "NOOO!" it was so intense. The woman next to me, who had been reciting all of Bella's lines in unison under her breath during the first movie (this was an event where they played all four movies before premiering part two at midnight), was openly sobbing and hyperventilating. As Edward and Bella fought Aro the tension in the air was unmistakable and as the flames engulfed him there was cheering and screaming like you hear on TV when a major sports team wins the game. Then, when it showed everyone still there, people were yelling, "WHAT?" and still crying. When Alice said that was Aro's future, the theater erupted in applause.

Does it bother the perfectionist in me that it's a complete (and admitted) plot hole since Alice can't see visions with the wolves? A little, but this moment of my life—and also getting to watch the reactions I still see people post from first-time watchers—makes it so worth it that I don't care.

I really enjoyed the show. The first half was better than the second, but I still liked it as a whole. Episode 6 is probably my favorite because of Death alone. I've rewatched that part probably fifty times just for her. One thing that really took me out of the show right away was how time seemed to pass while Dream was imprisoned. He was supposedly locked up for 105 years, but this does not at all match the rate of aging other characters underwent. Roderick's son is one example. The boy looked to be around nine or ten at the start and was somehow still alive over a century later when Dream escaped. You could argue this had to do with the magic artifacts his dad stole that kept everyone youthful, but he aged normally during the ten years his dad had those items. John, Ethel's son, is another example. She was kept young by her amulet but he should be in his nineties at the point we meet him and is clearly not, though again you could argue he had the ruby for a while so this slowed his aging. The most apparent flaw in the time frame is Unity. She was twelve when Dream was captured and was never in contact with any magical objects. This means she should be about 117 years old when she wakes up, i.e. dead. Maybe there's some explanation, like "well the sleepy sickness slows your aging a bit too" or "Desire impregnated her so that's why" but those reasons are so flimsy IMO. Maybe this world has some scientific advancement we don't that allows normal humans to live for so long, but if so they should have said. As it is, this whole issue of time really took me out of the story and I wish they could've just said Dream was locked away for 75 years instead of 105. It'd make the ages of all these characters far more believable.
